subject: [PATCH RFC fstests] generic: add a test for multigrain timestamps

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christoph Hellwig suggested exposing a flag in statx to indicate support for multi-grain timestamps, instead of relying on an explicit allowlist of filesystems.
reviews.raw_body:
Can we please expose the fact that multi-grain timestamp are supported
from the kernel?  This seems like it would be just one bit we'd need
in sttx or something similar.

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author agrees that an explicit allowlist might be the right approach and plans to explore adding a flag to stx_attributes.
reviews.raw_body:
I'd been resisting that, but maybe it's a good idea. I'll see what I
can come up with. We can probably just add a flag to stx_attributes?
-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch adds a test to ensure that multigrain timestamps are working correctly in Linux kernels. The test, called 'mgtime', checks that the mtime and ctime of a file appear to change even when there are multiple writes in quick succession. This is particularly important for filesystems like ext4, f2fs, btrfs, tmpfs, and xfs, which support multigrain timestamps but may not be universally supported on all filesystems. The test uses a loop to write to a file 1000 times and then checks that the mtime and ctime are different from the previous value each time. If the values do not change, the test fails.

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the multigrain timestamps are no longer tied to actual inode flags, specifically STATX_ATTR_DAX and STATX_ATTR_WRITE_ATOMIC, since their introduction.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, ever since STATX_ATTR_DAX/STATX_ATTR_WRITE_ATOMIC these don't
seem to be tied to actual inode flags any more.

reviews.author: Zorro Lang
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zorro Lang questioned the explicit allowlist approach, suggesting that it might not be the right solution for testing multigrain timestamps support across different filesystems.

Reviewer Zorro Lang pointed out a potential issue in the mgtime.c code where using the '-v' option would cause argv[1] to be set to '-v', and suggested checking optind instead, which is used to access the actual command-line arguments

Reviewer Zorro Lang suggested using the existing xfstests_statx() function from src/stat_test.c instead of statx(), citing potential support issues on older systems.

Reviewer Zorro Lang suggested changing the condition in the mgtime test from checking non-zero to <= 0, which could also detect clock rollback bugs.

Reviewer Zorro Lang noted that the existing test groups in doc/group-names.txt only include an 'atime' group, and suggested introducing a new 'timestamp' group to categorize tests for atime, ctime, and mtime; alternatively, sticking with the current 'atime' group is acceptable.

Reviewer Zorro Lang suggested removing the stale comment about cleaning up $TEST_DIR/test_mgtime_file.$$ in _cleanup by either defining a local _cleanup function or dropping the existing comment

reviewer suggested wrapping the multigrain timestamp logic into a _require_multigrain_timestamps() helper and noted that if there is a better way to probe filesystem type, it can be discussed later

Reviewer Zorro Lang noted that the patch does not handle the case where the file is closed and reopened, which would cause the multigrain timestamps to be reset, and requested the test be modified to account for this.
reviews.raw_body:
^^^^
                    2026 ?

---

If you use "-v" option, won't argv[1] be "-v"? Maybe you should check optind,
and use argv[optind].

---

statx() is a relatively new system call that might not be supported on older
systems. Perhaps you could refer to src/stat_test.c and use xfstests_statx() ?

---

It looks like this currently only checks whether the timestamp changed.
Changing the condition from checking non-zero to "<= 0" might can
also catch clock rollback bugs (even if that scenario seems unlikely:)

---

I just checked doc/group-names.txt and noticed that it only lists the 'atime'
group. I think it would make sense to introduce a 'timestamp' group. There
are already quite a few tests covering atime, ctime, and mtime in xfstests,
but they all seem to be lumped under the 'atime' group for now.

Of course, if you'd rather not deal with introducing a new group in this patch,
sticking with the 'atime' group for now is totally fine.

---

If you want to clean up "$TEST_DIR/test_mgtime_file.$$" in _cleanup, you
can define a local _cleanup function here. Otherwise, you can drop the
stale comment above.

---

We could wrap this logic into a _require_multigrain_timestamps() helper.
If there is a better way than probing FSTYP, we can always discuss
and update it later.

---

_exit 0

Thanks,
Zorro
